routes.title: Embroidery vs Screen Printing vs Sublimation vs Transfer | Irha Apparels
routes.description: Select an apparel decoration method by comparing artwork, fabric compatibility, coverage, hand feel, sampling and order-specific requirements.
routes.h1: Embroidery, Screen Printing, Sublimation and Transfer Printing Selection
routes.bodyText:
Embroidery, Screen Printing, Sublimation and Transfer Printing Selection

Decoration should be selected from the artwork, fabric, garment construction, colour count, coverage, intended use and buyer-approved appearance. No method is automatically correct for every product.

Embroidery

Embroidery creates a stitched surface and can suit logos, badges and selected decorative areas. Review stitch density, backing, thread colour, edge definition, garment stability and the effect of the embroidery weight on the fabric. A large or dense design may alter drape and comfort.

Screen printing

Screen printing can support solid graphics and repeat production on compatible fabrics. The ink system, colour separation, underbase, curing and desired hand feel should be reviewed for the fabric and artwork. Approve colour and placement on the intended garment rather than only on a screen image.

Sublimation

Sublimation is commonly considered for suitable polyester-based performance fabrics and all-over or panel artwork. The product pattern, colour management, print placement and cut-and-sew alignment must be planned together. It is not a general replacement for decoration on every fibre or dark finished garment.

Transfer printing

Transfer methods include different film, ink and adhesive systems. They can support detailed or multi-colour artwork, but the result depends on fabric compatibility, pressing conditions, stretch, surface texture and intended care. The exact transfer system should be identified and sampled.

Patches and combined methods

Woven, embroidered, printed, rubber or other patch directions can be reviewed where suitable. A design may combine methods, but thickness, attachment, wash behaviour and production sequence should be approved.

What the buyer should send

Vector or high-resolution artwork
Exact decoration dimensions and placement
Colour references
Fabric and garment construction
Intended use and care expectations
Quantity, colourways and size range
Any required testing or destination evidence

Approve a physical sample or strike-off suitable for the method. Decoration cost and timing depend on artwork, size, colours, material, setup and quantity, so they should be quoted against the actual brief.

routes.title: How Apparel Sampling and Product Development Work | Irha Apparels
routes.description: Follow a controlled apparel sampling process from requirement review and material selection to buyer comments, pre-production approval and bulk reference.
routes.h1: How Apparel Sampling and Product Development Work
routes.bodyText:
How Apparel Sampling and Product Development Work

Sampling is a decision and verification process. Its purpose is to convert the buyer's requirement into a garment that can be reviewed for material, measurements, construction, appearance, branding and packaging before bulk production is confirmed.

1. Requirement review

Send the product reference, technical pack or sketches together with quantity, colour, size, fabric, decoration, label, packaging and destination information. Identify any non-negotiable details and any areas where the manufacturer may propose an alternative.

2. Feasibility and material direction

The manufacturer reviews construction, available materials, trims, decoration compatibility and the proposed size system. Any substitution should be documented and approved rather than assumed. Commercial terms remain provisional until the workable specification is clear.

3. Artwork and technical confirmation

Confirm logo files, print or embroidery dimensions, placements, colour references, label text, care information and packaging artwork. Measurements should use a defined method and include a tolerance proposal suitable for the product.

4. Sample development

A sample may be used to assess fit, workmanship, visual balance, material behaviour and branding. The sample type and what it is intended to approve should be written down. One sample does not automatically validate every colour, size or decoration variation.

5. Buyer comments and revisions

Comments should be specific and measurable. Mark each point as approved, revised or still open. Keep the latest measurement chart, artwork and construction notes under clear version control so the bulk instruction is not assembled from conflicting messages.

6. Pre-production confirmation

Before bulk production, confirm the approved sample reference, final specification, quantity and size breakdown, material and trim approval, branding files, packing method, quality checkpoints and commercial terms.

7. Bulk-production reference

The approved documents and sample become production references. Any later change should be reviewed for its effect on price, material, timing, quality and packing before it is accepted.

Sampling cost, number of revisions and timing vary by product complexity, material availability and buyer response. These points should be agreed for the actual project.

routes.title: How to Choose GSM for Custom T-Shirts, Hoodies and Sweatshirts | Irha Apparels
routes.description: Choose fabric weight for custom T-shirts, hoodies and sweatshirts by reviewing composition, construction, finish, fit, sampling and buyer requirements together.
routes.h1: How to Choose GSM for Custom T-Shirts, Hoodies and Sweatshirts
routes.bodyText:
How to Choose GSM for Custom T-Shirts, Hoodies and Sweatshirts

GSM means grams per square metre. It describes fabric mass per area, but it does not by itself prove softness, strength, warmth, opacity, shrinkage performance or overall garment quality. Two fabrics with the same GSM can behave differently because the fibre composition, yarn, knit structure, brushing, compacting, dyeing and finishing are different.

Start with the intended product

Define whether the garment is a lightweight layer, an everyday T-shirt, a structured oversized style, a warm hoodie, a loopback sweatshirt or another specific product. Explain the target climate, retail position, fit and expected hand feel. A useful request describes the result the buyer wants instead of using GSM as the only quality instruction.

Confirm the full fabric specification

Record composition, knit or weave, target GSM, colour, finish, stretch direction, surface appearance and shrinkage expectations. For fleece and French terry, also confirm the inside construction. For rib components, specify where they are used and how their recovery should relate to the main fabric.

Review a physical sample

Approve fabric and garment behaviour together. Check drape, opacity, recovery, collar or rib stability, seam appearance and the result after the agreed care test. A small fabric swatch helps with hand feel, while a garment sample is needed to review fit and construction.

Keep quotation inputs connected

Fabric choice affects consumption, decoration compatibility, handling, packing and freight. Send the intended quantity, colours, size range, branding, packaging and destination with the material direction so feasibility, sampling and commercial terms can be reviewed for the actual program.

Practical RFQ checklist

Product type and intended use
Composition and preferred fabric construction
Target GSM as a direction, not a quality guarantee
Fit, measurement chart and tolerance proposal
Colour and finish requirements
Printing, embroidery or other decoration
Labels, hangtags and packaging
Quantity, size split, destination and requested trade term

Final material, MOQ, price and production timing should be confirmed only after the complete brief and available material options are reviewed.

routes.title: Clothing Tech Pack Checklist for Apparel Manufacturing | Irha Apparels
routes.description: Build a clearer clothing tech pack with product identity, materials, measurements, construction, artwork, labels, packaging and approval records.
routes.h1: What to Include in a Clothing Tech Pack
routes.bodyText:
What to Include in a Clothing Tech Pack

A clothing tech pack is the working product specification shared between the buyer and manufacturer. It should make the intended garment reviewable and reduce decisions that would otherwise be left to assumption.

Product identity

Give the style a stable name or reference code. Include front, back and relevant detail views. State the intended category, wearer group, fit and use. Record the document version and date so later comments are applied to the correct file.

Bill of materials

List the main fabric, rib, lining, interlining, mesh, elastic, thread, zipper, buttons, snaps, drawcord, eyelets, labels and packaging components that matter to the style. Describe composition, construction, target weight or thickness, colour and finish where known. Mark any item that may be proposed by the manufacturer.

Measurements and grading

Provide points of measure, measurement method, base size, size range, grade rules and tolerance proposal. A sketch showing exactly where each measurement is taken prevents different interpretations of the same label.

Construction details

Show seam, hem, pocket, collar, hood, cuff, waistband, closure, reinforcement and lining requirements. Note stitch appearance or construction only where it is important to the product. Use enlarged detail drawings for areas that cannot be understood from a flat sketch.

Artwork and decoration

Attach usable artwork files and define dimensions, colours, placement and method direction. State whether the requirement is embroidery, screen printing, sublimation, heat transfer, patching or another process, while allowing the method to be reviewed against the fabric and design.

Branding and packaging

Include neck label, size label, care label, country-of-origin information, hangtag, barcode or sticker requirements, polybag or other individual packing, folding direction and carton marks. Destination-market text and compliance requirements remain the buyer's responsibility unless otherwise agreed.

Approval record

Keep sample comments, approved revisions and open points in one controlled record. Do not rely on scattered chat messages as the final production instruction.

A tech pack can begin incomplete, but missing decisions should be identified before quotation or sampling. The final bulk specification should be the approved version rather than the first draft.

How to Source Private-label Lederhosen

A serious B2B enquiry should begin with the intended market, product construction, reference images or technical pack, target size range, branding plan and packaging needs.

Confirm the specification

Ask the manufacturer to confirm the proposed leather or alternative material, embroidery placement, lining, hardware, pockets, reinforcement, labels and packaging against an approved sample or written specification. Do not treat an illustrative website description as a production commitment.

Review the sample path

Define which details must be approved before production: measurements, fit, color, embroidery, trims, labels and pack presentation. Quantity, sample cost, production timing and delivery terms should be quoted only after the requirements are reviewed.

Verify the manufacturing partner

Request company details, recent product evidence relevant to your specification and a live factory video call where appropriate. Compliance or testing claims should be supported by current documents before they are used commercially.

Send a complete RFQ

Include destination, intended quantity, size split, reference files, required branding, packaging and requested trade term. This produces a more reliable quotation than asking for a generic unit price.

routes.title: OEM vs ODM vs Private Label Apparel Manufacturing | Irha Apparels
routes.description: Compare OEM, ODM and private-label apparel manufacturing and prepare the product, branding, approval and quotation inputs required for each route.
routes.h1: OEM vs ODM vs Private Label Apparel Manufacturing
routes.bodyText:
OEM vs ODM vs Private Label Apparel Manufacturing

The terms OEM, ODM and private label are often used together, but they describe different levels of buyer ownership and manufacturer development support. The correct route depends on how complete the product specification is and which decisions the buyer expects the manufacturing partner to help develop.

OEM apparel manufacturing

OEM is suitable when the buyer controls the product design and supplies an approved technical pack, physical reference, measurement chart, artwork or another detailed specification. The manufacturer reviews feasibility, materials, construction, decoration, sampling and production against that buyer-owned brief.

The buyer should clarify which details are fixed, which may be proposed by the manufacturer and who approves any substitutions or revisions.

ODM apparel development

ODM involves more development input from the manufacturer. A buyer may begin with a concept, reference direction or target market and require help turning it into a workable garment specification. The development route should still produce written, reviewable decisions for material, measurements, construction, trims, branding and packaging before bulk production.

ODM does not remove the need for buyer approval. Product ownership, artwork rights and confidentiality should be agreed for the actual program.

Private-label manufacturing

Private label generally means a product is manufactured for sale under the buyer's brand. It may use an OEM specification, an ODM development path or a selected existing product direction. Labels, care information, hangtags, packaging, decoration and carton marks must match the approved brand and destination requirements.

Information to send before quotation

Product references or technical pack
Intended quantity, colours and size split
Fabric and performance direction
Measurements, fit and tolerance expectations
Artwork and decoration placement
Label, hangtag and packaging requirements
Destination and requested trade term
Sample, revision and approval expectations

MOQ, sample cost, price, production timing and shipping arrangement depend on the actual product and order structure. They should be confirmed after the requirement is reviewed rather than presented as universal promises.

routes.description: Custom Dirndl manufacturing for Austrian wholesalers and brands with dress, blouse, apron, embroidery, labels, sizing and sample approval.
routes.h1: Wholesale Dirndl Manufacturer for Austrian Buyers
routes.bodyText:
Create coordinated Dirndl programs with defined silhouette, fabric, blouse, apron, trims, embroidery, size range, branding and packaging.

What Austrian buyers can source

Irha Apparels manufactures custom Dirndl dresses, blouses and aprons in Sialkot, Pakistan for importers, wholesalers, retailers, teams and private-label brands. Each program is reviewed against the buyer's specification rather than sold as a fixed retail product.

Mini, midi and long Dirndl silhouettes

Cotton, linen-look, velvet and other approved fabrics

Lace, puff-sleeve and custom blouse options

Satin, cotton, lace or embroidered aprons

A buyer-approved production workflow

Bulk production is not treated as an automatic next step. Materials, measurements, decoration, labeling, packaging, quantity and commercial terms are documented and approved before production commitments are made.

Requirement review covering product, quantity, materials, branding, packaging and target delivery window

Sample or pre-production approval before bulk production is confirmed

Quality checkpoints for measurements, construction, decoration and packing

Export and shipping terms agreed in writing for the buyer's destination

Supplying Austrian from Sialkot

Dirndl quality depends on the coordination of multiple components. Dress, bodice, blouse, apron, trims and sizing are reviewed as one approved set so bulk production follows the same reference.

Fabric and trim board approval

Bodice and skirt measurement review

Blouse and apron coordination

Retail-set packing requirements

Private-label presentation and buyer trust

The company is an experienced manufacturer and the website is newly built. Qualified buyers may request a live factory video call and discuss evidence needed for their own sourcing, compliance and approval process. Typical buyer profiles include Trachten boutiques, wholesalers, event suppliers, private-label fashion brands.

Custom woven labels, care labels, size labels and hang tags

Embroidery, screen print, DTF and other decoration reviewed by artwork and fabric

Buyer-specific packaging, folding and carton-marking requirements

Factory view available on a live video call for qualified buyers

Une fabrication conçue pour les acheteurs professionnels

Irha Apparels développe des vêtements de sport, des articles en cuir, du streetwear, des vêtements de loisirs et des programmes de marque privée à partir d’un cahier des charges, d’un dossier technique ou d’un modèle de référence. Chaque produit est étudié pour son usage, son niveau de qualité, sa présentation commerciale et son canal de vente.

Vêtements de sport et tenues d’équipe

Vestes et vêtements en cuir

Streetwear, sweats, T-shirts et ensembles

Les matières, mesures, couleurs, composants, techniques de marquage, étiquettes et emballages sont clarifiés avant la production. Les commentaires sur l’échantillon et les corrections convenues sont documentés avant toute validation de série.
